Voicing AI Ships "Knowledge Mesh," Anthropic Scrambles for Compute, Google Merges AI Mode Into Search

Today's top stories in AI + Product Marketing

1

Voicing AI Launches "Knowledge Mesh" — A Context Layer for Enterprise Agents

New infrastructure play: Voicing AI just launched Knowledge Mesh, a context layer that constructs, governs, and delivers organized knowledge to AI agents. The company says AI context platforms represent a $28 billion market in 2026, growing to $78 billion by 2030. The pitch: this isn't another chatbot — it's the substrate that makes agents actually useful.

2

Anthropic Scrambles for Compute as IPO Approaches

The Information reports that Anthropic has scrambled to line up cloud computing deals with SpaceX, Google, and others to meet skyrocketing demand for Claude Code and Cowork that "took the company by surprise this year." As the AI powerhouse gears up for a potential record-setting IPO (analysts float a $1 trillion+ base case), investors are asking: will that compute be enough?

Read on The Information →
3

Google Merges AI Mode Into AI Overviews — Organic Results Slide Down

Google confirmed AI Overviews now expand into AI Mode by default on some queries, loading the "Ask anything" box automatically. Organic results slide way down. Meanwhile, Search Console is rolling out new AI visibility reports and a toggle to block your content from AI Overviews, AI Mode, and Discover. Key stat from early data: conversational queries earn roughly half the click-through rate of short keyword queries at every position band.

Read on Search Engine Land →
4

Gartner: 40% of Enterprise Apps Will Embed AI Agents by End of 2026

The shift from AI assistants to AI agents continues to accelerate. Gartner now expects around 40% of enterprise applications to embed AI agents by year's end. Marketing agents can plan campaigns, generate content, schedule distribution, monitor performance, and adjust — while the marketer sets objectives and reviews output. The gap between having AI and having autonomous AI is closing fast.

Read on Admarp →
5

China's AI Giants Join PyTorch Foundation

Alibaba Cloud, Cambricon, and Ant Group have joined the PyTorch Foundation as members — Alibaba and Cambricon as Platinum members. This signals continued global momentum in open-source AI infrastructure, even as geopolitical tensions simmer. For enterprise buyers, the takeaway: the AI toolkit is getting more competitive, not less.

💡 My Take

Read this one: The Voicing AI story on Knowledge Mesh. We've spent 18 months talking about AI agents, but the infrastructure layer that feeds them context is where the real enterprise value will accrue. This is the plumbing that determines whether your agents are smart or stupid — and it's a $28B market that most PMMs aren't watching closely enough.
